---
title: "Solution: Closed-Form OLS with lm()"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

```{r load-packages}
library(tidyverse)
library(modelr)
library(broom)
```

## Task 1: Fit the linear model and decode summary()

```{r task1}
data("diamonds", package = "ggplot2")

mod_linear <- lm(price ~ carat, data = diamonds)
summary(mod_linear)

# From the output:
# Intercept: -2,256.4
# Slope (carat): 7,756.4
# Residual standard error: 1,549 (on 53,938 df)
# R²: 0.8493
# F-statistic: 3.041e+05 on 1 and 53,938 df, p-value: < 2.2e-16
```

## Task 2: Interpret the slope

```{r task2}
slope <- coef(mod_linear)["carat"]
cat("Slope:", round(slope, 2), "\n")

# Interpretation:
# A 1-carat increase in diamond weight is associated with a $7,756 increase
# in price, on average. This is the marginal price of one additional carat,
# not controlling for any other quality attributes.
```

## Task 3: Fit the log-log model

```{r task3}
mod_loglog <- lm(log(price) ~ log(carat), data = diamonds)
summary(mod_loglog)

# From the output:
# Intercept: 8.449
# Slope (log(carat)): 1.676
# Residual standard error: 0.2956 (in log-USD units)
# R²: 0.9330
```

## Task 4: Interpret the log-log slope (price elasticity)

```{r task4}
elasticity <- coef(mod_loglog)["log(carat)"]
cat("Price elasticity of carat:", round(elasticity, 3), "\n")

# Interpretation:
# A 1% increase in carat weight is associated with a 1.676% increase in
# diamond price. Since elasticity > 1, price grows faster than weight —
# doubling carat more than doubles price. This is consistent with the
# economic scarcity of large gem-quality stones.
```

## Task 5: Compare models

```{r task5}
r2_linear <- summary(mod_linear)$r.squared
r2_loglog <- summary(mod_loglog)$r.squared

cat("Linear model R²:", round(r2_linear, 4), "\n")
cat("Log-log model R²:", round(r2_loglog, 4), "\n")

# The log-log model explains 93.3% of variance in log(price) vs 84.9% for
# the linear model on raw price. The improvement has two sources:
# (1) The price-carat relationship is a power law, which is linear on the
#     log scale but curved on the raw scale — the log transformation
#     corrects for model misspecification.
# (2) The log transformation stabilises variance: the raw price residuals
#     fan outward (larger errors for more expensive diamonds), while
#     log-price residuals have more constant spread.
```

## Task 6: Tidy the log-log model with broom

```{r task6}
tidy(mod_loglog)
glance(mod_loglog)

# The log(carat) coefficient has by far the largest t-value (>> 100),
# meaning we can reject H₀: β₁ = 0 with overwhelming certainty.
# This confirms that carat weight is an extremely strong predictor of
# log(price) — removing it would catastrophically worsen the model.
# The intercept t-value is also very large: the baseline log-price
# (at carat = 1, i.e., log(carat) = 0) is precisely estimated.
```
